# CobolSharp Developer Log

A chronological narrative of building a production COBOL compiler from the ISO/IEC 1989:2023
specification, targeting .NET. This log captures the thinking, decisions, failures, breakthroughs,
and lessons learned — intended as source material for a series of articles.

---

> **Ordering: DESCENDING — newest entry FIRST.** The latest entry is the `## Entry` block immediately below this line; the oldest is at the end. Add a new entry by inserting it directly under this note.
>
> **Timestamps (required, going forward):** every NEW entry's header carries a real date+time stamp —
> `## Entry NNN — YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ — Title` (24-hour local time; get it from `date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"`, e.g.
> `2026-06-09 13:01 PDT`). The time gives the per-day granularity older entries lack, so same-day entries are always
> ordered/renumber-able. (Entries 001–511 predate this rule — many are undated and none have a time; left as-is.)

## Entry 1561 — 2026-09-06 11:56 PDT — Notes 8–9: PB767–PB769 and PB771 (the registrar's body replaces the landing's stopgap), PB772–PB778, PB780 and PB782 filed, PB710 retired as refuted, six owners appended, the SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS figure note repaired from the rendered page

Three registrars filed the defects the last two days of landings surfaced, each grepping the register before allocating, and between them they refused four ids to existing owners — which is the point of a registrar. Registrar 8 measured that the documented landing pathspec `":!STATUS.md"` makes `git add` exit 1 while staging everything else (PB767, a false failure signal rather than a lost stage), that the process-observation drift test blesses an unbounded private launcher in the legacy CLI test (PB768), that the register's Analyses view lists eighteen landed notes as backlog (PB769), and that RELATIVE and INDEXED files establish no §9.1.15 lock against another run unit while their CLOSE rewrites the file from the OPEN snapshot, losing the other run unit's writes with both sides reporting '00' (PB771 — the body that ships here re-derives the note train 18's lander had to write as a stopgap so the three PARTIAL rows had a live claimant; same id, same rows). It also rendered PDF page 322 and measured the SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS figure mechanically: the underlined set is exactly SYMBOLIC, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL and IN, with no rule under CHARACTERS, so the figure note that said otherwise and the grammar comment that claimed a repair are both corrected. Registrar 9a filed PB772 (the lander briefs tell a lander a code must be in the catalog "and" the generated diagnostics doc, as if a rendered file were a second register), PB773 (§12.4.5.2 rules 11 and 13 have no enforcement site and no structural home in the key-rule table), PB774 (COBOLNET0901's message names only user-defined words where the rule also bars system-names), PB775 (six agent briefs hand out unguarded filtered `dotnet test` lines, and a valid filter naming no test also exits 0), PB776 (eight PHASE-14 command blocks name three test classes that exist nowhere, two of them gating exit criteria) and PB777 (the WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase has no edition gate and its 2002 date is unsourced). Registrar 9b filed PB778 (the EDITING clause's literals are the narrow literal rule, coupled with PB568 which needs character-1 narrowed on the same lines), PB780 (an adjudication for the blank whole-language row SR-13.10.3-2) and PB782 (the shipped compiler's exit-code contract — 0, 65, 66, 70, a forwarded child code — has no test; the only such test covers the legacy exe and dies at P15); it retired PB710, whose premise that untokenized §8.9 words are never screened PB301 refuted by measurement, and it appended PB555 (literal-4 is never bound and SR27 is unenforced), PB642 (the guard's compare arm still cannot tell a truncated normalization from a difference — pipefail is already set; nothing asserts the output), PB763 (the rule-catalog warning for §9.3.6), PB655 (the REPORTS reserved-word row is not inert) and PB503, which is open for a defect the optional-word relaxations already fixed. Nothing here changes the compiler; the register now holds 819 well-formed items and both citation audits are at zero.

Plan §9's reference moves to #60, #59 becomes the previous record, #58 drops off, and #61 at train 18's head must be all green with zero flips.

## Entry 1559 — 2026-09-06 11:45 PDT — LANDING TRAIN 18, finished by a second continuation lander: the condition-name subject's class read ONCE and for a group too; ORDER given a lexer token so the DUPLICATES phrase stops borrowing `cobolWord`; a conflict marker in a tracked file made a red unit test; the §9.1.15 file lock DERIVED rather than a clause's side effect — and its three rows recorded PARTIAL, not CONFORMS, because the evidence is sequential-only

**This train was landed by TWO landers, and the second one changed a verdict.** The first was killed by an API session limit with all five cluster commits made and the gate never run; the orchestrator preserved its uncommitted edits as a WIP commit and dispatched a fresh lander onto its branch. The continuation fast-forwarded, dissolved the WIP commit rather than promoting a subject that says "WIP" onto main, kept the one edit that was real work (PB740's row correction), discarded the killed lander's half-applied traceability-inventory hunk, and re-applied all four verdict batches with `record_verdicts.py` on the merged tree — the standing rule for an inventory that has been touched by a merge. Four clusters landed, none dropped: **PB728+PB575, PB704, PB735, PB740**, plus **PB761**, the reconciliation the train itself forced and which rode in on PB740's branch.

**PB728 + PB575 — the condition-name subject's class, read once, for a group too.** A level-88 whose conditional variable is a `GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL` or `GROUP-USAGE BIT` group was classified from the group's RAW `PICTURE`, which is null for a group, so the group form took the alphanumeric collating sequence where the identical elementary twin took the national one — §8.8.4.2.1 13) says a national group item shall be treated as an elementary national item for comparison, and §13.18.29.4 1) b) says the same of a bit group. PB575 is the same rule at a different site: every Format-3 VALUE guard in `DataBinder.BindCondition` read the same null picture, so the class funnel that draws COBOLNET0899/0898 on the elementary twin fell through silently on the group. Both now read `DataItem.OperandPic` — D20's ONE operand-category reader. The implementer's sweep found ELEVEN arms where the note named three, each measured before and after: a wrong answer on a single-VALUE national or bit group, a silent acceptance on VALUE THRU, a missing EC-RANGE-INVALID on an alphanumeric group via `ThruMember`, `ALL B"1"` repeated to ONE position on a bit group, `SET … TO TRUE` on national and bit groups throwing `NotImplemented.Value<string>` at run time and on an alphanumeric group emitting C# that DID NOT COMPILE (CS0029) — all three collapsed onto one group-image store `FromImage` — EVALUATE WHEN THRU over a national group, and `CLASS __CLASSIFY.For`. One fact in the note was wrong and is corrected in it: `CollateArgFor(null)` returns `, __COLLATE`, Alphanumeric per §8.8.4.2.3 SR2, which is why the alphanumeric-group control was preserved rather than changed. ⛔ This row had to be RECONCILED at the landing: PB741 landed alone hours earlier and had independently fixed the level-88 membership and EVALUATE THRU sites through its own PAIR classifier `CollatingSelection.ForComparison` / `CollateArgFor(left, right)` — the one-argument overload is deleted on main. The reconciliation keeps PB741's pair classifier as the ONE comparison-class mechanism and brings this row's sweep in on top of it; both goldens are kept because they assert different arms (`2023/pb728_condition_name_group_subject_class`, fourteen assertions over two alphabets via ALSO and proven load-bearing — swapping alphabets flips 6 of 14 — and PB741's `2002/pb728_level88_group_usage_collating`), as are both drift tests, plus three negatives and the semgrep rule `cobolnet-condition-category-from-raw-picture`, which is declared, fires on its testdata and is now part of `verify.py`'s seven. Rows `SR-13.18.63.3-24` and `SR-13.18.63.3-29` PARTIAL → CONFORMS.

**PB704 — ORDER gets a token, so the DUPLICATES phrase stops borrowing `cobolWord`.** `SORT … WITH DUPLICATES IN ORDER` was rejected at 2002, 2014 and 2023 with COBOLNET0901 on ORDER while compiling clean at 85. The printed general format was RENDERED and MEASURED (PDF 774/775): only DUPLICATES is underlined, so ORDER is an OPTIONAL word (§5.2.3), never a name — but the grammar spelled it as a `cobolWord`, and `VersionConformancePass.VisitCobolWord` screens IDENTIFIER occurrences POSITION-BLIND, so the §8.9 reservation funnel read the format's own word as a user-defined one. The fix is in the borrowing rule, not an exemption: an `ORDER` lexer token plus a `cobol-words.json` nameSlot row, from which the DERIVED gate emits both `{userWordHere("ORDER")}? ORDER` and the `reservedGatedWord` twin — so `01 ORDER PIC X.` is still legal at 85 and still draws COBOLNET0901 at 2002+ — with `sortDuplicatesPhrase : WITH? DUPLICATES IN? ORDER?`, an explicit `orderTableClause`, the `orderTableAhead()` text predicate DELETED and the funnel's ORDER TABLE exemption deleted with it (PB101 had patched one of ORDER's two positions and left the other — the two-arm dispatch, again). An under-rejection closed with it: `WITH DUPLICATES IN <any word>` no longer parses. ⛔ Two things the note asserted were FALSE and are corrected: ORDER is not a REQUIRED word, and there is no MERGE twin — §14.9.24.2 has no DUPLICATES phrase at all. `DESIGN-frontend-grammar.md` had asserted that ORDER "has NO lexer token, arrives as IDENTIFIER, and no gate can reach it"; both halves were false and that unmeasured sentence is what let PB704 through, so the document is corrected in the same change set. The sweep was re-run on the corrected axis — "§8.9-reserved at any edition", token or not, where PB693's finisher had asked "reserved AND has a token", which is exactly why ORDER escaped — and six borrowed reserved words measured clean at 2023. Goldens at all four editions plus `2023/pb704_sort_duplicates_gr3_arms`, the negative `pb704-order-as-data-name`, ORDER added to the 85 acceptance lane, two `OptionalWordSubsetDriftTests` rows and a strict-2002 `SpecPinnedNistTests` case that asserts the ABSENCE of 0901 and the presence of 0873. Row `GR-14.9.40.4-3` → CONFORMS, all three arms.

**PB735 — a conflict marker in a tracked file is now a RED unit test.** An implementer had committed a merge with four unresolved conflict hunks into `scripts/spec/audit_grammar_optional_words.py` and no gate saw it, because nothing in the wave-local gate imports that script. The fix is structural: `ConflictMarkerDriftTests` takes its population from `git ls-files -z` and nothing else, so the gitignored GnuCOBOL corpus is excluded BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a path exclusion that would rot; it scans bytes for all FOUR marker forms including diff3's `|||||||`; it applies the company rule to both dividers because `=======` is a legal setext underline; it runs a CRLF/LF Theory whose LF arm was MISSING in the first draft and was found by the implementer's own self-review; it costs 370 ms over 7,304 text files; and its watchdog FIRED end to end on a planted hunk in a tracked file, so its silence is evidence. `TheSweepActuallyReadsTheTrackedTree` is the standing population invariant. The same rule was written into the lander and implementer brief templates as a staged assertion gated on OUTPUT rather than on `git diff --cached --check`'s exit code — because DEVLOG.md is CRLF and `--check` calls every one of its lines trailing whitespace — and `SKILL.md` §3 now FORBIDS `git stash` outright, since the common dir is shared and one worktree's `git stash list` shows other agents' WIP. Register hygiene rode with it: PB736 and PB588 are ONE defect, so PB588 is `retired` with a pointer and its evidence folded into PB736; `kb/Work.base`'s three open-work views excluded only `landed`, so the first retired note would have shown as open — the views are fixed and `work.py` now guards the class (a view hiding any terminal status hides all), with the failure branch fired once. A seventh private process launcher was found and rewritten onto `ProcessObserver.ObserveOrThrow`. No inventory rows.

**PB740 — the §9.1.15 file lock is DERIVED, not a clause's side effect — and its rows are PARTIAL.** Two CLAUSE-LESS connectors on one ASSIGN that Table 19's arbiter permits (OPEN INPUT then OPEN EXTEND) were refused by the OS handle posture with `B-OPEN=30` and the record never written, while a `SHARING WITH NO OTHER` connector's handle ADMITTED an external writer. The posture a connector's own handle carries is now derived from `FileLockPosture.For` — the §9.1.15 union over the set of connectors open on the physical file — with `FileRegistry.PostureOf` SPENDING `For` instead of re-implementing it (`For` had been reachable only from the drift tests: a dead lookup is also an unverified one), `SequentialConnector.OpenReader`/`OpenWriter` as the single spellings of the two handles, `AdmitsAnotherWriter` a bit test and `OtherAdmittedModes` an iterator. Its finisher also REPAIRED the checkpoint's own origin/main merge, which had silently DROPPED `pb739_shared_extend_write` from BOTH conformance manifests. ⛔ **The three rows `GR-9.1.15-1/-2/-3` are recorded PARTIAL, not CONFORMS, and that is the landing's own correction to the implementer's batch.** The evidence is SEQUENTIAL-ONLY. Re-derived at the landing rather than inherited: `RelativeConnector` and `IndexedConnector` hold no long-lived host handle at all — their only other host call is `HostFile.Probe` — and reach the physical file solely through `RecordFraming.ReadStore`/`WriteStore`, which take their streams from `HostFile.OpenAuxiliary` (`src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/FileSupport.cs:265`), fixed at `FileShare.ReadWrite` with no share parameter at all; the CLOSE-side `WriteStore` is `FileMode.Create` and rewrites the whole store from this run unit's in-memory copy. So an INDEXED file opened `SHARING WITH NO OTHER` is not protected from another run unit, and another run unit's records are silently discarded with both sides reporting '00'. §9.1.15 3) — "The successful opening of a file establishes a file lock for the applicable sharing rules, thereby preventing other run units from opening that file with incompatible sharing rules", validated with `cite.py --check` — is written over *a file* and is not qualified by organization. The IN-RUN-UNIT half (Table 19) IS arbitrated for every organization and is what PB740 fixed; the OTHER-RUN-UNIT half is carried only by the sequential connector's own handle. CONFORMS would have closed the row on a verdict with a known hole, so the keyed half is **kb/Work PB771**, filed live, claiming the three rows. That note is not optional bookkeeping: with the rows PARTIAL and no live note naming them, `DefectiveRowCoverageDriftTests.EveryDefectiveRow_IsClaimedByALiveWorkNote` was MEASURED RED at the landing — "3 defective row(s) with no live work note (of 4348 examined)". `GR-14.9.51.4-19` and `GR-14.9.27.4-4` were re-recorded through the same batches because the symbols they name moved; `GR-14.9.27.4-4` stays PB321's claim. Owner question 20 — whether a CLAUSE-LESS connector should protect its physical file from external PROCESSES at all — is recorded in the note and is unanswered.

**PB761 — the national THROUGH stage is discharged, not widened.** Not in the manifest: this is the reconciliation the train forced, committed separately so a bisect lands on it. Row 1 extended the COBOLNET0899 `national-through-range` stage to the GROUP shape as its stated "honest interim", and on this tree that turned PB741's LANDED golden `2002/pb728_level88_group_usage_collating` red — a golden that asserts a national GROUP THROUGH range compiles and answers correctly under `ALPHABET REV-NAT FOR NATIONAL IS N"ABC"`, with its expected values derived from the spec. Extending a "recognized but not yet implemented" stage over demonstrably implemented behaviour is the sharpest available statement that the stage is FALSE. Declining both shapes would be a capability regression and a new refusal of conforming source; gutting PB741's golden would be changing valid COBOL to dodge a compiler bug; so the stage is DISCHARGED. It was measured before the decision was taken, with the guard disabled and the tree rebuilt: the `GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL` subject and its elementary `PIC N(3)` twin answer alike and BOTH flip when the national alphabet is reversed, so §8.8.4.2.9's national program collating sequence is genuinely consulted and the range is not riding the native UTF-16 ordinal — `ConditionRenderer` has emitted `CobolString.Compare(read, lo, __COLLATE_NAT)` for this shape since PB678 put `__COLLATE_NAT` live. The citation the stage carried was the defect: §13.18.63 SR31 governs the `IN alphabet-name-1` phrase and never makes a national THROUGH range unimplementable. `docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md` loses the `national-through-range` descriptor row, and the negative `pb761-national-through-alnum-literals` pins what SR31 actually forbids.

**The train.** Five cluster commits (`712bdb2d` PB728+PB575, `4e89eda3` PB704, `26f98b95` PB735, `aa177af7` PB740, `90a4afa2` PB761) plus one closing commit carrying the four verdict batches, PB771, the DEVLOG and plan §0. GAP **2780 → 2777** on an unchanged denominator of 4,348 (`build_inventory.py --check`: 4348 rules, 4348 rows, GAP 2777) — 3 and not 6, because PB740's three rows are PARTIAL. No diagnostic code was claimed: COBOLNET1892–1899 were reserved across the four rows, none was used, `docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md` was regenerated from `DiagnosticCatalog` and came back byte-identical to what the clusters had already produced, and the next free code is still COBOLNET1859. The manifest audit the train's own history demanded — the train-16 and PB740 merges each silently dropped a golden once — is CLEAN on all five manifests: 45/45 at 85, 216/216 at 2002, 62/62 at 2014, 533/533 at 2023, 857/857 negative, zero unlisted, zero orphaned, zero duplicates, and every negative program carrying its `*> reject-at:` first line and its `.err` sidecar. `semgrep/verify.py` PASSES with no count above baseline and all seven rules firing on their testdata; both citation audits are at zero findings; `work.py check` reports 807 work items, all well-formed; the conflict-marker sweep PB735 landed is silent over the tracked tree, which is the first landing it has ever gated. ⛔ **One claim in the train's own manifest was FALSE and the gate caught it**: PB735's row names `WorkRegister` as a `dotnet test` term, and `filter_population.py` — PB708's guard, landed one train earlier — calls it DEAD: it matches no test in Conformance, Unit or Characterization, because the `work.py` view guard is a python self-test and not a vstest. The gate REFUSED to run rather than reporting a clean verdict line under a false claim, which is exactly what that guard was built for. Ten further terms are Unit-only and were named INERT against a Conformance filter (CobolWords, ConflictMarker, ProcessObservation, OpenTable19, SharedExtend, HostFile, Table20, CobolFileLock, FileLockPosture, GrammarDiagramGenerator); every one of them runs in the UNFILTERED full-Unit leg, so the union Conformance filter was trimmed to its sixteen live terms. **The gate, one build for the whole train:** Conformance filtered `Passed! — Failed: 0, Passed: 4757, Total: 4757, Duration: 12 m 29 s`; the FULL unfiltered `Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit` assembly `Failed! — Failed: 2, Passed: 22884, Total: 22886` — the two reds being `ExternalCorpusPopulationDriftTests.TheCensus_NamesEveryPopulationAndItsProgramCount` and `.SweepExternalPopulation_EqualsTheDifferentialsCommittedCaseCount`, the documented worktree shape (the GPL GnuCOBOL corpus is not present in an agent worktree) and no cluster's; Characterization `Passed! — 33 of 33`; the legacy `CobolSharp.Tests.Integration` assembly `Passed! — Failed: 0, Passed: 503, Skipped: 1, Total: 504`; NIST re-run standalone `Passed! — Failed: 0, Passed: 353, Total: 353`, NC215A included. `GrammarDiagramGeneratorDriftTests.Generator_RunsClean` passed inside the loaded full-Unit run, so PB736 did not fire and nothing needed re-running in isolation.

## Entry 1558 — 2026-09-06 09:36 PDT — Battery #59 at trains 15–16 + PB741's head: every compiler leg green (NC215A restored) and seven differential flips attributed — six conforming acceptances and improvements from the optional-word relaxations and the key rules, one an illegal ALPHABET literal phrase a correct relaxation exposed, whose over-acceptance predates the trains and is filed as PB770; all seven rows re-baselined by hand; plan §9 reference moves to #59

Battery #59 was cut at PB741's solo landing over trains 15 and 16, and it is the first battery since #56 with every compiler leg green: the full Conformance assembly at 6192 of 6192 with NIST NC215A restored, the unit assembly clean, the guard's witnesses and audit clean. It carried seven differential flips, and an adjudicator attributed each by rendering the general-format pages rather than reading the transcription. Five are conforming acceptances the optional-word families landed — the word TO in INITIALIZE's ALL TO VALUE, the VALUE clause's WHEN, SET, TO and IS, the word CHARACTERS in SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, and CLASS overlaps that the ALPHABET rule's scope leaves legal — and one is PB699's file-control key rules rejecting a program GnuCOBOL rejects item for item. The seventh looked like a regression and was not one: an ALPHABET literal phrase with duplicate characters, illegal under §12.3.7.3 SR14 a), that both compilers had rejected and this one now accepts — but the pinned compiler from before the trains accepts the identical duplicates once the IS it falsely demanded is supplied, so the old agreement was coincidental, a rejection of legal source hiding an under-rejection. That is PB770: the ALPHABET clause's alphanumeric literal-phrase arm never received the validator its national twin has, the deferral is written into a code comment that promises a diagnostic later, an unrecognized code-name falls through into an alphabet made of its own letters, and a 65,536 ordinal that the range check admits is masked into a 256-wide table with a measurably wrong collating order — the two-arm dispatch for the fifth time. Two of the accepted programs now compile and abort at run time on a feature PB455 already owns. All seven rows were re-baselined by hand in the verdict manifest, plan §9's reference moves to #59, and #60 at train 17's head must be all green with zero flips.

## Entry 1556 — 2026-09-06 09:17 PDT — LANDING TRAIN 17, finished by a continuation lander: REWRITE's six alternate-key obligations and the declined annex as descriptor DATA; an as-if OPEN that renders the whole OPEN; three rows PB339 made true; every filter TERM put back to vstest; a shared EXTEND release placed and numbered at the WRITE; and the last ten optional words, with the audit at zero

**This train was landed by TWO landers.** The first was killed by an API session limit after committing rows 1
and 2 and part-way through row 3; the orchestrator preserved its uncommitted work as a WIP commit and dispatched
a fresh lander onto its branch. The continuation read the WIP against the row's expected share — 3 files
`+214/−4` where PB737's own work is 4 files `+238/−28`, the missing file being the traceability inventory the
standing rule discards anyway — and, rather than promote a partial checkpoint into a landing commit, reset to
row 2's boundary and redid row 3 cleanly. No `WIP` subject reached main. That is the checkpoint protocol working
as designed: one step lost, nothing repeated.

**Row 1 — PB702 + PB709 (`d578b720`).** PB702 verdicted two claimable rows from evidence rather than from the
note's summary of them. `GR-14.9.35.4-24` — REWRITE's alternate-key repositioning — turned out on a re-read of
the PRINTED rule to carry SIX obligations, not the two the note recorded; the existing `altkey_suppress_when.cob`
reaches only WRITE-time suppression and the READ/START path, so a new golden `2023/l1_rewrite_alt_key_suppress`
(`L1RWSUP`) makes a key ENTER suppression, LEAVE it back into its duplicate set (returning LAST, per GR24 b), and
puts two records at the suppression value of a key declared without DUPLICATES; its twenty expected lines were
computed from the spec before the first run and matched byte for byte. `SR-12.4.5.2-7` had both halves
re-measured live — COBOLNET1810 at 85, COBOLNET1811 at 2023 — plus the two ACCEPTING-arm goldens the note never
named. PB709 was WIDER than filed: §4.2.6 (Annex A.3, processor-dependent) was cited where §4.2.7 (Annex A.4,
optional) governs, and the difference is NORMATIVE — §4.2.6 alone carries the mandatory warning mechanism and the
"not required to diagnose syntax errors within" licence, which three VALIDATE sites were leaning on and which A.3
does not grant. Commit/rollback appears in BOTH annexes, so the annex is a SET, not a scalar. The fix is
structural: `[Flags] DeclinedAnnex` + `DiagnosticDescriptor.Annex` + a derived `PostureClause`, eleven declined
descriptors tagged, and `DeclinedFacilityAnnexDriftTests` (five facts, one of them a cross-check against
`docs/CONFORMANCE.md`'s §2/§5 registers) proved red by flipping COBOLNET1580. Thirteen sites corrected — eight in
code, five in docs — plus a correction banner on the Wave-H scout section, because `docs/CONFORMANCE.md` was the
SOURCE of the error: its §4 bullet, its §1 and its header all filed VALIDATE under §4.2.6.

**Row 2 — PB714 (`e5e25c55`).** `SortEmitter`'s implicit OPENs for SORT/MERGE USING and GIVING files rendered no
SHARING override, so §14.9.40.4 GR12 a) / GR15 a) and MERGE's §14.9.24.4 GR7 a) / GR12 a) never took effect —
`cite.py --find "as if an OPEN statement"` returns exactly those four, and their four CLOSE twins were already
correct. Measured: `IN-ST=00` and three records read where `'61'`, `'42'` and zero records were required. The fix
is ONE renderer, `SortEmitter.EmitImplicitOpen(file, mode, sharing, ruleComment)`; a non-null sharing renders
`CobolFile.OpenShared`, the same entry an explicit `OPEN … SHARING` uses, and the OTHERWISE arm renders the PLAIN
entry because GR12 a) continues *"the absence of the SHARING phrase means that the sharing mode is completely
determined by the SHARING clause"* — PB316's two arms, where a phrase-bearing entry would register a
record-locking participant the standard never made one. `RuntimeApi.FileOpenInput` and `FileOpenOutput` are
DELETED, so the drift is compile-enforced. A sibling fell out of the same read: the implicit OPEN also skipped

On this rebuild thirty-four ids disappeared, eleven appeared, and SIX adjudicated rows kept their id while their text changed underneath — `GR-14.9.20.4-L2.2` held PB415's PARTIAL for *"The REPLACING phrase is specified…"* and would have carried it silently onto *"If the category of the receiving-operand is object-reference…"*. `added`/`removed` compare ids and `subject` is the rule block's subject, so nothing in the pipeline could have seen it. The guard was proved to fire before it was trusted (a flipped stored digest gives exit 1 naming `SR-14.9.41.3-6`), and the landing states its migration explicitly precisely because the guard is silent on the rebuild that installs it. One verdict genuinely moved, in the honest direction: `RV-15.95.4-1` CONFORMS → PARTIAL, because `1) b) 5.` is PARTIAL and r1 as a whole cannot read CONFORMS now that the obligation is counted inside it. PB697's premise, meanwhile, was false in the implementation's favour: the render of the printed format shows the brace group's two arms as un-underlined placeholders realized by ONE grammar rule, so the arm was never missing — what is absent is the operand DOMAIN, which §4.2.6 licenses for the unclaimed Annex A.3 item 40 SOURCE phrase, with the warning obligation landing where it belongs, on `SR-14.9.41.3-7` (PB358). Owner decision PB55 ("the rule is the unit") was applied, not re-decided.

**PB339 — `READ … INTO` sent the whole record AREA, and the sentence's second half was not implemented at all.** §14.9.30.4 GR4 b) and §14.9.34.4 GR5 b) are the same sentence twice, and both halves were wrong. The SIZE half: the emitters sent the space-padded area and a comment argued the two were *observationally identical* — true for a left-justified receiver, and the discriminator is JUSTIFIED, because §13.18.32.4 GR1 truncates the LEFTMOST characters of an over-long sender, so five bytes read into `PIC X(10) JUSTIFIED RIGHT` arrived as ten spaces. The GROUP-MOVE half was simply absent: a FORMAT 2 FD with an elementary `01` was EDITED into `XXBXXBXX` and CONVERTED into `999.99`, where §14.9.25.4 GR4 requires the receiving area be filled *"without consideration for the individual elementary or group items"*. One mechanism answers both — a structural `BoundCurrentRecord` operand built only by `SequentialIoEmitter.IntoSender` and rendered only by `OperandText.CurrentRecordImage`, with `MoveClassifier.IsGroupSender` gaining the GR4 b) designation arm and `VaryingRecordInfo` finally learning which RECORD FORMAT was written, because GR4 b) conditions on the word VARYING and GR16 sits under the Format 2 heading, so a rule keyed on that word previously had nothing to key on. §13.18.43.4 GR16's closing sentence makes a ZERO byte count legal and it was measured reachable. The `… FROM` arms are NOT the mirror and deliberately keep the plain MOVE, with §14.9.51.4 GR5 / §14.9.35.4 GR7 / §14.9.32.4 GR4 as the evidence. The design decision landed as **D21**: its D19 slot had been taken twice while the work was in flight, by train 14's PB692 and train 15's PB683.

**PB695 family 2 — four optional words in `CobolData.g4`, and a printed bracket ORDER no optional-word audit can report.** Family 2 was four rows, not the five the dispatch counted: the fifth was the confirmations table's NOT_A_DEFECT row that family 1's own tool fix had already retired. `codeSetForPhrase` FOR, `dynamicLengthClause` LENGTH and `initializeCategoryToValue` / `initializeDefaultPhrase` TO are relaxed, every underline re-measured as second reader off the raw rectangles. The sibling sweep, run with family 1's blind spot flipped, found `valueClause`'s WHEN, SET and TO required against a printed bracket carrying exactly one rule, under FALSE — and then found something an underline audit structurally cannot see: format 3 prints `[ IN alphabet-name-1 ]` BEFORE `[ WHEN SET TO FALSE … ]` and the grammar had them reversed, so the PRINTED spelling was a COBOL0001 while an order no format prints was accepted. §5.2.6.2 makes bracket order part of the format; swapped. The relaxation then forced a restructuring, which is the shape of this row: with THEN and TO optional, `INITIALIZE X DEFAULT` becomes legal, DEFAULT rides `cobolWord`, and ANTLR's greedy operand loop ate it — one rejection traded for another — so INITIALIZE now has its own `initializeOperandList` carrying the §8.9 guard `valueClause` already carries for PROPERTY, narrow by design so the shared `dataReferenceList` keeps its separate question. One residue is reported rather than papered over: `IN` cannot be relaxed, because §13.10.3 SR2 lets a constant-name stand where a literal may, so an `IN?` would be a dead branch. Forty-five probes, twenty-nine failing before and zero after; the audit's list goes 12 → 8, and the eight are exactly family 3. PB695 stays OPEN.

**PB338 — a governed READ that decided AFTER it retrieved, and a design doc that said it had to.** Record-lock governance on the keyed organizations ran after the physical read, so an unsuccessful governed READ (`'51'`) left the file position indicator advanced and SILENTLY SKIPPED the record it failed on, where §14.9.30.4 GR10 a)/d) require the position and the key of reference to be UNCHANGED. Measured with two `SHARING WITH ALL OTHER` connectors: the conflicted READ returned `'51'` and the NEXT sequential READ returned the SECOND record. GR11 a)'s prior-lock release was the second half and a textbook two-arm defect — the rule ties the release to EXECUTION (§12.4.5.9.4 GR6 is explicit), the standard says "at the completion of the SUCCESSFUL execution" in 11 b) and says neither in 11 a), yet READ gated it on success at both call sites while the governed MUTATING verbs in the same file released unconditionally. The root was in the design doc: `COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN.md` D17 asserted that a keyed walk learns its record BY READING IT, which made a pre-read check look impossible. It is not, and D17 is corrected in place. The fix is peek-then-commit on all three organizations, with the SELECT rules split from the COMMIT so peek and read call one selection and cannot drift; `FileRegistry.ReadShared` peeks, the post-read leg is deleted, a new `ReadKeyedShared` OWNS the Format-2 retrieval, and `ReleasePriorRecordLocks` becomes the ONE §12.4.5.9.4 GR6 site for all four verbs where there had been four copies. A lock-ceiling denial (`'53'`/`'54'` — this connector's own count, not GR9's conflict) invalidates the position per GR18 so the next sequential READ is `'46'`, and that discrimination has its own golden. Nine arms were enumerated rather than assumed: START is already correct by §14.9.41.4 GR3, and ADVANCING ON LOCK stays post-read because GR22 re-executes the read. Two landing repairs finished what the report described but the branch had not: the now-callerless `RuntimeApi.FileReadKeyed` — the ungoverned Format-2 renderer PB683's own invariant comment three lines above it forbids — was removed, and that comment corrected to name the entry that replaced it.

**PB713 — the second handle was the root, and the spec chose the fix.** `OPEN EXTEND` on a sharing-active LINE SEQUENTIAL file threw an unhandled `IOException`: the registry opened the EXTEND writer and THEN seeded the existing-record count from a SECOND handle, outside `FileConnector.Open`'s try, so a host refusal escaped where §14.9.27.4 GR1 admits only an I-O status and GR25 requires the file be left unaffected — a conformance failure twice over, since the runtime manufactured a refusal for an open §9.1.15 item 3 allows and then let it escape. Two fixes were available and §14.9.51.4 GR19 decides between them: the base is *"the records present in the physical file when it was opened"*, and an `OPEN EXTEND` writes nothing, so the count taken before the writer exists and the count at the OPEN's completion are the same number — seeding first is not merely permitted, it is the shape with no second handle in it, which is the root. The share mode then became a STRUCTURE rather than a fifth ternary: `HostFile.OpenConnectorStream` writes the §9.1.15 posture once where four call sites had open-coded it, `HostFile.OpenAuxiliary` covers bookkeeping reads, and every host-path open under `Runtime/IO` now routes through one of the two — including the fixed-attribute sidecar, whose refused read had been silently skipping §14.9.27.4 GR10's `'39'`. The drift test bans any other host-path open statically and was proved red 12 of 23 on the pre-fix tree.

**PB699 — nine key rules that only a VERB could trigger, replaced by one table on the entry.** The KEY syntax rules of a file control entry were screened by `KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile`, memoized, at five call sites, so a program with only `OPEN`/`CLOSE` violated every one of them in silence — keys under OCCURS, RELATIVE plus ACCESS RANDOM with no RELATIVE KEY, a RELATIVE KEY inside the file's own record. Probing the rest of the clause family found two more the note did not have, and the worse of them was not a missing diagnostic at all: an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY naming a WORKING-STORAGE item was silently DROPPED from `FileModel.AlternateKeys`, so the file was built with fewer access paths than the entry declared and every index-aligned list downstream was out of step with the written clauses; a RECORD KEY naming an undefined item produced the false message "indexed file has no RECORD KEY clause", about a clause the program plainly wrote. Two inherited citations were wrong in two places each — §12.4.5.13 carries no syntax rules; the required-clause rule is §12.4.5.2 SR10 and the unsigned-integer and not-in-a-record rules are §12.4.5.13.3 SR2/SR3. The fix is ONE table, `FileControlKeyRules.cs`, screened once per DECLARED file from `DataBinder.ResolveFiles`, where an ABSENT clause is an operand with a null name so "clause required" and "operand breaks a rule" are one row kind with no second dispatch arm; `KeyedValidateFile`, its memo and all five call sites are deleted. The nine negatives are ENTRY-ONLY programs, which is the discriminator against the existing `pb354-*` cases that contain a READ and would pass under the old shape. Two rows deliberately earn NO verdict, and the gate is why: PARTIAL was recorded first and `DefectiveRowCoverage` rejected it, because a non-resolving verdict is a PROMISE that something owns the remainder and PB699 is landed, so the promise would have been orphaned on arrival — the rows go back to carrying nothing, which is exactly true, and the remainder is note-ready. `COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN.md` D19 now states one decision instead of two, folding train 14's PB692 material in with this row's criterion: decidable-from-the-clauses goes in `BindFileControl`, needs-a-resolved-item goes in `ResolveFiles`, neither goes on a verb.

**The train.** Six clusters, seven commits plus this one; nothing dropped. Rows 4,371 → **4,348** and GAP 2810 → **2788**, and the two halves are different in kind and must not be read as one number: thirteen of the twenty-two are the DENOMINATOR moving, a transcription repair with no compiler change behind it, and nine are actual progress (PB339 one, PB338 four, PB713 one, PB699 three). `build_inventory.py --check` exits 0 on the result. The gate ran once for the whole train over the union of the six rows' terms — thirty-nine `FullyQualifiedName~` terms — plus, per the amendment after batteries #56 and #57, the FULL `Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit` assembly and the legacy `CobolSharp.Tests.Integration` assembly: Conformance **4227/4227**, Unit **22,564 of 22,566**, Characterization **33/33**, legacy Integration **503 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed**, NIST **351 of 352**. Semgrep held at 427 and both citation audits report zero. The two Unit reds are the known `ExternalCorpusPopulationDriftTests` pair, which cannot pass in a worktree without the GPL corpus, and the one NIST red is `NC215A` — train 14's PB678 collating regression, PB741, whose blocking fix is in flight elsewhere; neither belongs to any row here. The train's own two reds were real and both came from row 3's base predating train 15's PB688, which gated `ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL` to COBOL-2023: family 2's CODE-SET artefacts are COBOL-2002 programs carrying a LINE SEQUENTIAL file, and a keep-both resolution of the 2014 corpus manifest re-added a program PB688 had MOVED to 2023. The first was repaired by taking family 3's already-corrected golden verbatim; the second is the more general lesson and got its own commit — **a union resolution of an append-only list has to read what the other side DELETED, not only what it added**, and `Manifest_CoversEveryProgram_NoOverlap` is what caught it. One report claim did not hold on today's tree: PB338's report says `RuntimeApi.FileReadKeyed` was deleted and it was not, which left an ungoverned Format-2 renderer standing under the comment that forbids it.

## Entry 1549 — 2026-09-06 05:00 PDT — Battery #58 NOT GREEN at train 14's head, attributed: a real wrong answer reached main — NIST NC215A's numeric-against-figurative comparison under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE lost the sequence when PB678 folded the comparison's collate argument into the SORT-key classifier (PB741, a blocking fix in flight); the guard's NIST leg never saw it because it drives the legacy compiler (PB750); the one differential flip is PB692's improvement, re-baselined; plan §9 reference moves to #58

The full Conformance assembly's NIST differential failed NC215A on `SEQ-TEST-GF-6` — `IF NINE-DU-9V0-1 < SPACE` under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE printed `FAIL*` where the golden requires `PASS` — and the adjudicator reproduced it in isolation, then bisected it by reading and by build: green at train 13's head, red at PB678, the train-14 cluster that resolves a collating sequence per key class for SORT and MERGE. Its fold of the comparison's collate argument routed through the new classifier whose numeric arm answers the SORT-key question, where a numeric key takes no sequence, when the comparison question was being asked, where §8.8.4.2.5 makes a numeric operand against an alphanumeric one an alphanumeric comparison under §8.8.4.2.7's program collating sequence and §12.3.7.4 GR7 k) puts unspecified characters above the specified ones; a minimal discriminator answers the same comparison two ways depending on whether the space is spelled as a figurative or a literal. That is one classifier serving two questions, and it is being split as PB741, a blocking cluster. The finding under the finding matters as much: the guard's NIST leg reported 353 matches and a clean audit in the same battery because `guard-fast.sh` and `guard.sh` drive the legacy compiler, whose project graph does not even contain the greenfield code generator, so every "NIST MATCH" line a battery has ever printed was evidence about the oracle, not about COBOL.NET — the greenfield NIST evidence has always been the Conformance assembly's differential partitions, and PB750 records the leg for redirection. The battery's one differential flip is an improvement: PB692's new screen rejects DYNAMIC and RANDOM access on a sequential file as §12.4.5.5.2 SR2 requires, GnuCOBOL agrees, and the row is re-baselined by hand. ## Entry 1548 — 2026-09-06 05:00 PDT — PB718–PB722 and PB724–PB726 filed by three registrars that verified every claim first (PB720's premise false — the row-existence guard already exists; PB721 re-shaped — a zero minimum record size is legal and the real defects are a false conformance row and an unscreened RECORD clause; PB724 closed on filing; five duplicate findings folded into their owners and their ids burned); the printed standard's own dropped glyphs left faithful; the §12.4.5.10.2 figure note and the project's conformance citation corrected

PB718 counts fifty lettered sub-items outdented to column zero at printed page breaks, measured rather than assumed (every correctly indented lettered item in the standard has exactly one blank line before it, thirty-eight of the fifty candidates sit at a wider seam) plus seven lines with two ordinals welded together; it needs no migration of its own because the catalog's ordinal regexes are digit-only. PB719's ordinal-form drift in §14.9.10.4 starts at the first general rule, not the fifth, and the first six resolve to an empty path. PB721's premise was false the other way: a zero minimum record size is explicitly legal by §13.18.43.3 SR7, the inherited citation had answered a different question, and what the note now files is the conformance statement's row 43 claiming a minimum of one against a compiler that round-trips zero on both organizations, and a RECORD clause binder that screens none of the clause's six integer rules. PB722 quotes the refuted claim in an inventory row's notes and shows the probe that evidenced it could not fail either way. Of the nine findings train 14's lander listed, five were already in the register from the same reports a day earlier, so their new evidence went into the owners and the files were deleted with the ids burned; PB724 closed on filing (COMMIT and ROLLBACK are gated, and the bare word those editions accept is a paragraph name); PB725, PB726 and PB728 are the genuinely new ones, the last a measured wrong answer on a level-88 over a national group. The third pass filed what the resumed implementers had left: PB732, an undefined word as a VALUE operand that is never resolved, larger than reported because a Format-1 item VALUE prints the word silently where the level-88 form crashes in Roslyn; PB733, the VALUE clause's FALSE and IN phrases ungated at 85, where the whole of Annex E names neither and the introducing edition cannot be derived in the repository, so deriving it is the note's first work item; PB734, a printed brace made optional so `INITIALIZE X TO VALUE` behaves as ALL, which must combine with family 2's relaxation of the word TO; PB735, the committed conflict markers, with the fix sited in both briefs and a tracked-file drift test rather than a hand-kept exclusion; PB736, the diagram generator's wall-clock wait asserted ahead of the drift assertions; and PB738, an owner decision — a content-stream scan of all 1,261 pages found exactly five places where the published standard itself drops a character, and the transcription reproduces them faithfully, so the convention for recovered readings is the owner's to choose. Two documents were corrected on discovery: the §12.4.5.10.2 figure note said RECORD was underlined where the render proves it is not, and the mission line in the project's own instructions cited the user-documentation criterion as the definition of a conforming implementation, where §4.2.1 is.

## Entry 1547 — 2026-09-06 04:37 PDT — Landing train 15: six clusters, GAP 2815 → 2810, and one verdict that had to be un-landed

**PB691 + PB144 — the WRITE arm of a three-time silent drop, and what "tolerated" actually obliges.**
`SequentialIoBinder.BindWrite` never called `w.writeInvalidKey()`. The phrase parsed, bound nowhere, and neither
imperative ran — at every edition and on both severity axes, with no diagnostic. It hid because the
`writeInvalidKey` sub-rule was consumed by the KEYED binder only: the two-arm dispatch with one arm fixed, this
repo's most reproducible defect shape, and the third time this exact family produced it (PB144 for REWRITE,
PB334 for READ). §14.9.51.3 SR2 states it as a format rule — *"If the organization of the write file is
sequential, format 1 shall be specified"* — so the prohibition lives in the DIAGRAM, and PDF pages 785–786 were
RENDERED rather than read off the OCR: Format 1 carries ADVANCING + END-OF-PAGE and no INVALID KEY bracket,
Format 2 the reverse. The screen is `StatementValidation.ScreenForbiddenPhrase` on the existing COBOLNET1720
descriptor, routed through `EditionContext.Removed` (error under strict, warning with an unchanged bind under
`--permissive`), with the REWRITE sibling given the same shape. The deeper finding is that *"the phrase is dead
under `--permissive`"* had been over-read into a licence to DROP it: §9.1.14's final rule has two items, and
item 2 — *"control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement or to the imperative-statement
specified in the NOT INVALID KEY phrase if it is specified"* — makes the NOT INVALID arm **live** on every one of
these statements, because each of them succeeds. Only the INVALID arm is provably dead (§9.1.13.5 names a
relative or indexed file in each of `'21'`–`'24'`). So both sequential arms now bind the pair, and `EmitInvalid`
moved from `KeyedIoEmitter` to `SequentialIoEmitter` — the declared home of the file-I/O common services the
keyed emitter already consumes — with the four keyed call sites repointed; exactly one `EmitInvalid` now exists.
Two negative fixtures, six behavioural tests, and a one-sided D9 sweep over the 459-program NIST corpus
(`COBOLNET1720 hits: 0`, the detector first proved able to fire). At the landing the COBOLNET1720 descriptor,
`BoundStores` and the D9 section were all resolved as the UNION with train 13's PB334 — the code now serves SIX
rules, and the design doc's "Four syntax rules" lead and "One code, five rules" line were corrected with it.

**PB693 — a hand-set flag where a derivation belonged.** `scripts/gen-cobol-words.ps1` emitted every reserved
word carrying `nameSlot: true` as a bare alternative of `cobolWord`, the user-defined-word slot, unless a
hand-set `reservationGated` flag said otherwise — and the flag was set on FIVE words. `UNLOCK` and 51 siblings
were therefore accepted as user words at 2002+, so a period-less `UNLOCK F1` after a `MOVE` was swallowed as two

twice. ⚠ The one gate red was attributed at the ROOT rather than suppressed: `validateStatusStage` had borrowed
`cobolWord` for the KEYWORDS FORMAT/CONTENT/RELATION that §13.18.62.2 underlines, so the new gate rejected legal
VALIDATE-STATUS source; a sweep of ~45 such sites found FORMAT to be the only §8.9 word with a lexer token a
rule expected `cobolWord` to match, and it got its own token arm. Two inherited clause numbers were re-derived
and corrected (§5.2.3 → §5.2.2, §4.2.6 → §4.2.7).

**PB703 + PB364 — the rule's boundary is the CLAUSE, and the register is now one register.**
`DataBinder.ResolveFileCollating` screened §12.4.5.7.3 SR8 with a `HashSet` hoisted OUTSIDE the loop over the

size the two arms of §14.9.51.4 GR26 appear to overlap. Printed page 792 confirms the transcription is faithful,

ALL-FILES rules and Format 1 prints ADVANCING, the retry-phrase and the WITH LOCK bracket together. The

Measured `B=ALPHA|00` → `BST=51`. ⛔ Recorded as **D20**, not the D18 the implementer wrote: train 13 holds D18

one as required; every underline was re-measured on the folios. The six siblings — currencySignClause WITH,

keyed on `ctx.FOR()` would otherwise have switched off with nothing failing), and OBJECT-COMPUTER's

**The train.** Six clusters, one build, one gate, six commits plus this one. Bases ASCENDED across the rows
(973460ba, 979b670c, then four at 2c8e32cb), so every row predated trains 13 and 14 and each conflict was
resolved by keeping BOTH mechanisms and re-deriving the seam: the COBOLNET1720 union above; `BoundStores`

## Entry 1546 — 2026-09-06 04:03 PDT — Battery #57 NOT GREEN at c34f01ad, all three findings attributed to train 13 and repaired: the legacy integration test's `START … KEY IS IX-KEY` was illegal COBOL (§14.9.41.2 prints the relational operator unbracketed) and PB332's tightening rejects it correctly; both differential flips are improvements (PB352+PB354's SR2 rejection, PB332's optional USE words) and are re-baselined by hand; PB717 filed; the lander brief now gates the full Unit assembly and the legacy Integration assembly; plan §9 reference moves to #57

Battery #57 was cut at train 13's head plus the seven note and ledger commits after it, and its first launch died in phase 0 on a corrupt reference assembly the interrupted afternoon had left in the battery worktree; a wipe of that worktree's build outputs and a relaunch produced a full run: every compiler leg green, the guard's witnesses and NIST audit clean, and three findings, which an adjudicator attributed by inspection rather than by bisect, since battery #56 two commits earlier was clean and train 13 is the only grammar change between them. The guard's legacy integration leg failed to parse `START IX-FILE KEY IS IX-KEY` — and the standard, rendered at folio 754, prints START's KEY phrase with the relational operator unbracketed, so `IS` alone is an optional word before an operator that is required; the test had been passing on a grammar that accepted an unprinted spelling, PB332's tightened rule rejects it correctly at every edition, and the one line now reads `KEY IS EQUAL TO`, with the same three assertions passing. The two differential flips are both improvements: `syn_file:459` is now rejected with COBOLNET0862 because PB352+PB354 turned §14.9.41.3 SR2 into a real screen, and GnuCOBOL rejects it too; `syn_misc:1152` is now accepted because the old USE rule demanded the word PROCEDURE, which §14.9.49.2 prints unlined, and PB332 relaxed it. Both rows were re-baselined by hand in the verdict manifest, whose own header calls regeneration a deliberate act and never a fix for a red. The generalizable lesson is PB717: the optional-word drift test measures what a format must accept and is structurally blind to what a tightening newly rejects, and the only suite that compiled the removed spelling runs in the guard, not in any per-commit gate — so the lander brief now requires the full Unit assembly (train 13's lesson) and the legacy Integration assembly (this one) on every train. Plan §9's battery reference moves to #57; battery #58 at train 14's head must be all green with zero flips.

## Entry 1545 — 2026-09-06 04:03 PDT — PB711–PB716 filed from the resumed implementers' reports, each claim re-verified before filing: PB712's runtime premise did not hold (the grammar spells the WRITE ADVANCING phrase twice, accepting an unprinted spelling and rejecting the printed BEFORE AFTER); PB713 reproduced as a crash; PB714 traced end-to-end; PB715's audit blind spot measured; PB716 the SPECIAL-NAMES switch entry that swallows a trailing keyword as a device name

The five "note-ready" findings the resumed implementers left in their reports went through a registrar that verified each before writing it, and two of them changed shape in the verification. PB712 was reported as the runtime discarding an end-of-page raised by the first of two advances in one WRITE; the printed page (folio 785) shows the choice indicators enclosing only the words BEFORE and AFTER, with one ADVANCING and one operand outside them, and Annex E.3.3 says both words are allowed together — so the report's `BEFORE ADVANCING 4 LINES AFTER ADVANCING 0 LINES` is an unprinted spelling the grammar accepts because it spells the whole phrase twice, while the only printed spelling of the combination, `BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING 4 LINES`, is rejected as no viable alternative; with legal source the end-of-page condition fires correctly, so the loss is real but unreachable, and PB712 is filed as the grammar defect, rejecting legal source and accepting illegal source at once. PB713 was reproduced rather than inferred: the shared OPEN attempt opens the EXTEND writer with read-write sharing and then seeds the base through `File.ReadLines`, which asks for share-read and dies with the exact stack the report predicted, and the varying arm's three-argument stream constructor defaults to the same share, so "very likely" became confirmed. PB714 was followed from the sort emitter through the runtime façade to the registry, where a null sharing override silently keeps the program's own mode, and its MERGE twins were bounded by asking the citation tool for every rule that says "as if an OPEN statement" — four rules, one emitter. PB711 found no descriptor to correct: COBOLNET1599's text is a bare literal at the emit site with a verbatim copy in a design evidence file, and its 1600 twin is worded correctly. PB715 measured the audit's blind spot live — ten candidates on one clause, none of them the FOR that the rule still demands — and in probing the harm found a different one, filed as PB716: the implementor-switch entry of SPECIAL-NAMES is one optional-everything rule whose minimum spelling is a bare word, so `CLASS DIGITS IS "0" NATIONAL IS MYMNEM.` binds NATIONAL as a device (the binder says so in its own diagnostic), accepted at every edition with no gate involved; the dropped attribute is not yet visible in output only because the CLASS clause's FOR arm never reaches codegen, a second gap named in the note's siblings, which is why PB716 and PB695's FOR relaxation must land together. The register stands at 762 well-formed items; the code audit at zero.

## Entry 1544 — 2026-09-06 03:22 PDT — Landing train 14: PB678 · PB350 · PB692 · PB346 · PB676 · PB688 (GAP 2820 → 2815)

**PB678 — the SORT/MERGE comparator selected by the key's CLASS, and two defects the note did not have.**
§14.9.40.4 GR5 and §14.9.24.4 GR5 resolve TWO collating sequences per statement — the alphanumeric one for keys
of class alphabetic and alphanumeric, the national one for keys of class national, "each separately determined"
— and the compiler carried ONE. PB327 had removed the FD/SD record gate that kept national keys away from it, so
a file SORT with a `PIC N` key silently mis-ordered; the table-sort twin still staged loud behind a comment
citing GR5b (the PROGRAM-collating-sequence precedence step, not the class rule — the sub-item was INHERITED,
and re-deriving it is what this change owes to rule 1) and naming a gate that no longer existed. The re-probe
found the site carried more than the note claimed: the key WINDOW was `ImageWidth`-sized over an image whose
basis PB327 had made BYTES, so a `PIC N(1)` key covered only its high byte — U+0000 for every Latin national
character — and three distinct keys compared EQUAL, returning the release order in the NATIVE case too, not just
under a declared alphabet. And the same dispatch was wrong one class over: a BOOLEAN key took the alphanumeric
weights, where GR5 names a sequence for neither class boolean nor class numeric and §8.8.4.2.8 compares boolean
operands "by their boolean value, regardless of their usage" — an `ALPHABET … IS "10"` inverted every bit
position. The fix is one classification, `CollatingSelection.Of` (`Binding/CollatingModel.cs`), and one resolved
PAIR, `SortCollation`: the binder resolves both halves by GR5a then GR5b independently and CARRIES the national
one (it used to validate alphabet-name-2 and throw it away, correctly, while no reachable program could observe
it); `BoundSortMergeKey.Class` replaces the `bool Numeric` bit and keys read `OperandPic` (D20) and `ByteWidth`;
`CobolSort.KeyColumns` holds a sequence PER KEY and decodes a national key's UTF-16BE byte pairs back to
national positions through `CobolBits.NatReadWindow` before comparing, because §8.8.4.2.9 compares positions;
`TableCompare` dispatches on the class through `AsNat()`, `AsBits()` and `AsImage()`, so a national or bit GROUP
key is the elementary operand §13.18.29.4 GR2b/GR1b makes it, and the `SortBinder.cs:176` loud stage is DELETED.
Two inline copies of the same class→sequence ternary in `ConditionRenderer` were folded onto
`EmitContext.CollateArgFor` rather than joined by two more. Two things fell out of the work: `CobolSort.Sort` and
`Merge` no longer take collating arguments at all — `Init` is the ONE §14.6.6 r5 statement-start snapshot, and
the second mechanism made "the store holds null" mean both "native was snapshotted" and "nothing was" — and
`BoundaryImageChannelTests`, the drift test that holds the one-reader law for group images, gained the
`AsNat`/`FromNat` pair it had never covered since PB327 created it. Goldens:
`2023/pb678_sort_national_key_collating` (eight legs including MERGE's own; three deliberately different orders
so no leg can pass for another's reason), `2002/pb678_table_sort_key_class` (GR5b, the statement-overrides-program
case, a boolean key with patterns chosen only after the obvious ones proved non-discriminating, and a national
GROUP key agreeing with the elementary one) and `negative/pb678-sort-collating-for-forms-at-85` (COBOLNET0872, a
gate that guarded nothing observable until the phrase started being carried); both positives proven RED by
corruption. `GR-14.9.40.4-5` and `GR-14.9.24.4-5` CONFORMS; no diagnostic code claimed from the 1842–1843 range.
The self-review's sweep left three findings note-ready for the register (ids are centrally allocated, so the
lander does not mint them): SORT's own `WITH DUPLICATES IN ORDER` is

## Entry 1504 — 2026-09-05 07:15 PDT — Landing train 8: five clusters in one landing (PB647 · PB300 · PB305 · PB303 · PB316)

**PB647 — one returned value, one rounding decision, and ROUNDED stops being a no-op on the float family.** PB623 (train 7) made the arithmetic and MOVE channels compute the same exact binary64 expansion; what still split them was the MODE. `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble` hard-coded NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO at a working scale while `CobolFloat.ToScaledUnchecked` had always taken the receiver's mode at the receiver's scale, so `MOVE FUNCTION SQRT(3) TO S` gave 1.732050807 into a `PIC 9V9(9)` and `COMPUTE S = FUNCTION SQRT(3)` gave 1.732050808 — one returned value, two landings, which §15.4.1 forbids outright — and `FUNCTION SQRT(0.9999999999)` into `PIC 9V9` split across a whole tenth. **In plain words for the owner: the ROUNDED phrase was doing NOTHING on the entire §15.4.1 floating-point intrinsic family** — `COMPUTE S ROUNDED` and the no-phrase `COMPUTE S` both answered 1.732050808 — and native `**` carried the identical defect; both are fixed here, and the float landing now takes the STATEMENT's rounding mode. Neither was in the note. A COMP-2 item holding the identical binary64 was already correct in all four positions, which is the measurement that identified this as the repo's recurring two-arm shape with one arm fixed — and the fixed arm was already in the file: `NumericRenderer.Divide` asks whether the value it computes IS the value transferred to a single resultant identifier (`_outermost`) and answers in two arms, and `Align` states the same for every other float→fixed intermediate. `ReceiverContext.FloatLanding(finalTransfer)` now decides the landing's SCALE and MODE together — the resultant identifier's scale with the statement's own mode when the value IS the transfer (§14.7.4.1's "truncation is relative to the size provided for the resultant identifier", §14.7.4.3 rule 2's "as if ROUNDED MODE IS TRUNCATION"), which is exactly §14.6.8.2 rule 4's MOVE landing, and the capped working scale with TRUNCATION when it is not; `FloatEdited` keeps a floating-point numeric-edited resultant out of the final-transfer arm. Landing AT the receiver's scale makes the store's rescale the identity, so the double rounding goes too, and §14.7.4.3 rule 7's PROHIBITED raise had to move INTO `FromDouble` — which fixed an unfiled defect where the same statement raised into `PIC 9V9` and stored silently into `PIC 9V9(9)`. The implementer did not inherit the codebase's `§14.7.7 rule 3 NOTE 1` justification: the text is real and `--check`s, but the rule opens "When standard-decimal or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect", so under native arithmetic it is a real clause answering a different question — everything new cites §14.7.4.1 and §14.7.4.3 instead, and hazard H2 is retired with its derivation in NUMERIC design D20. **Blast radius, measured rather than estimated: the whole corpus moved ONE golden in two lines.** `2023/pb65_codomain_clamp` is re-derived from the exact expansions and GAINS six ROUNDED legs, because truncation can never leave a codomain the double is already inside — PB65's clamp had been held open by a green test that no longer exercised it. **PB300 — one lexer token, two harms, and a hand list retired where a structure belongs.** The file-control `PADDING CHARACTER` clause parsed at EVERY edition with nothing reading it, so `SELECT F1 … PADDING CHARACTER IS SPACE.` was accepted silently at `--std 2023`, where the word occurs NOWHERE in the standard (grep: zero hits; §8.9's list runs PACKED-DECIMAL then PAGE with nothing between; §12.4.5's clause subclauses are §12.4.5.4 through §12.4.5.15 and none is PADDING); and the same token refused `01 PADDING PIC X(3).` at 2014/2023, where §8.9 leaves the word free — legal COBOL rejected with a bare COBOL0001. **In plain words for the owner: `docs/CONFORMANCE.md` carried NO row for PADDING, so there was no owner determination to follow, and the clause was IMPLEMENTED to its edition window rather than declined** — registry row `padding-character-removed-2014` gated at `VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitPaddingCharacterClause` (COBOLNET0902 strict, warning permissive), the rule kept parsing at every edition so the gate can NAME it. **PB253 — the arithmetic mode decides the container, and it is asked first.** `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat`
tested the RECEIVER SHAPE before the arithmetic mode, so under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` — and under
2002's plain `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD`, which `ArithmeticModes.IsDecimalEngine` also selects — the SDIDI arm
below it was unreachable for every receiver-less or float-receiver reference and a raw binary64 escaped. §15.4.1
is unconditional: "the returned value for numeric and integer functions is contained in a temporary standard
data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect", and §8.8.1.5.1 makes the mode "a
method of evaluating an arithmetic expression, an arithmetic statement, the SUM clause, **and certain integer
and numeric functions as specified in 15.4.1**" — the function itself, not only its use as an operand. §15.4.1's
last paragraph exempts the VALUE, never the CONTAINER, and the arm that ran in every mode was licensed by
§15.4.1's NATIVE-mode sentence — a real clause answering a different question. The harm was not a rendering
difference: `MOVE FUNCTION TAN(a)` landed 16331239353195368.96 while `COMPUTE r = FUNCTION TAN(a)` landed
16331239353195370.00 for the SAME call, and `FUNCTION RANDOM(7)` split 0.3832204692918902784 /
0.38322046929189024 — two returned values for one function and one argument in a single run, which §15.4.1
forbids by name; `DISPLAY FUNCTION SIN(1E-20)` printed `1E-20` where the SDIDI's item-92 text is
`0.00000000000000000001`. The fix is the ORDER, made STRUCTURAL rather than positional: one method became three,
`RenderFloat` now reads the mode and nothing else, and the D16 receiver-shape arms moved to a mode-blind
`RenderFloatNative` that cannot pre-empt the container rule — `num.StandardDecimal` is read at exactly one place
in this family. It moves the whole residue at once: ACOS, ASIN, ATAN, COS, SIN, TAN, LOG, LOG10, RANDOM, every
`Float: true` catalog row the standard-mode arm had not already claimed. The sweep asked "which arm did you fix"
of every sibling receiver-shape test in the numeric renderers — `CombineCore`, `Power`, `Landed` and
`ConditionRenderer` were already mode-first; `RenderFloat` was the one site not keeping the ordering
`COBOLNET_NUMERIC_DESIGN.md` D3 already states for the whole engine, and that doc's prose-family paragraph was
wrong in the same way the code was ("converting into expressions per §8.8.1.5.2 r1" — the OPERAND case only),
so it is corrected in the same change set. Three goldens at all three editions the rule reaches
(`pb253_prose_float_standard_container` 2002, `pb253_prose_float_sdidi_container` 2014 + 2023), each proved to
FAIL against the pre-fix compiler, plus `StandardModeReturnedValueContainerDriftTests`, whose fixture table is

`RV-15.89.4-1` PARTIAL → CONFORMS. No diagnostic code claimed.

**PB254 — a TOTAL function was inside a PARTIAL function's landing, and the wrong-answer half was in the lane

everything.** The directive was applied by ONE mechanism, the post-lex token retype, which can reach a word only
when the lexer makes it a keyword token; `DESIGN-cobol-words-directive` §2 asserted that the only words without a
keyword token type are intrinsic-function names, and `CobolKeywordTokens` asserted in its own summary that "every
reserved word and context-sensitive word is a literal lexer token". Nothing measured either claim and both were
false. Measured against ISO §8.9 ∪ §8.10 (552 words): 447 were in the token map, **17 are lexed but were invisible
to it** — ANTLR publishes a literal NAME only for a token defined by exactly one literal, so
`ZERO : 'ZERO'|'ZEROS'|'ZEROES'` and `PIC : 'PICTURE'|'PIC'` publish none — and **88 are no token at all**,

naming the renamed keyword, and `UNDEFINE "ANYCASE"` still ate the user's own data item as the keyword, switching
on case-insensitive currency matching with no diagnostic. The fix is the second mechanism, once, for the whole
class: `CobolWordsMap.Resolve` is the ONE reading of §7.3.10.4 GR2/GR3/GR4 and every by-name classifier calls it —
`IntrinsicBinder.KeywordWordOf` (the funnel every §15 phrase word is read through, so TRIM, FIND-STRING,

rule resolves without a hand-maintained list, and the de-reserve retype now matches the token TEXT because one

## Entry 1478 — 2026-09-05 02:44 PDT — Landing train 4: PB233 + PB598 + PB237 + PB238 onto main in one landing — the CALL statement's exception partition, its argument classification and its program-prototype registry, plus the VALUE size sentences that stopped binding a condition-name (GAP 2906 → 2893)

**PB233 — the CALL statement's GR3h/GR3i partition, and the activation boundary that makes it decidable.**
`kb/Work/PB233` said a CALL written with only `NOT ON EXCEPTION` swallowed a failed activation, and that the same
unfiltered catch routed EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND into the ON EXCEPTION phrase that §14.9.4.4 GR3h item 1 excludes.
Both reproduced on a fresh build. Probing them turned up a THIRD instance of the same mechanism that neither the
note nor the inventory rows had seen, and it is the one that named the root cause: a CALL whose callee is
*successfully activated* and whose callee's own inner CALL then fails ran the ACTIVATOR's `imperative-statement-1`
and let the run unit finish with exit 0 — which GR3i forbids in one sentence ("after control is returned from the
called program the ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored"). The emitted `try` spans the callee's entire
execution, so the CALL site had no way to tell a GR3b–f activation failure from an exception escaping the callee;
a family filter on the arm would have fixed the symptom the note named and left that one standing. So the boundary
became explicit. `ProgramTable.CallProgram` now marks `CobolCallException.ControlTransferred` on anything escaping
`inst.Call`, and every emitted arm filters on `!ControlTransferred`; the mark is monotone, so a failure deep in a
call chain is an activation failure for exactly one CALL site and post-transfer for every site above it. For
"escaped from `Call`" to *be* GR3g's test, GR3e's external-conformance check had to leave the callee body — GR3e
makes "the program call … not successful" and precedes GR3g's transfer of control — so it is now
`ICobolProgram.DescribeExternals()`, a default-no-op ABI member the boundary calls before `Call`. On that footing
the CALL emits three arms instead of two conflated ones, one per fact GR3h routes on: the enabled
EC-PROGRAM/EC-EXTERNAL arm (status set, then the phrase or the declaratives), the enabled non-family arm (status
set, then the declaratives ALWAYS — item 2's second disjunct, which had no implementation at all), and the
un-enabled family arm (the phrase only, and no status set, because item 1 carries no checking-enabled qualifier
while §14.6.13.1.1 does). The phrase arms key on `c.OnException`, never on the NOT phrase: §14.6.13.1.3 #1 admits
only "a conditional phrase without the NOT phrase". Item 2's second disjunct needed a binder half too, and that
is the part the row's own notes had mis-scoped: `EcBinder.QueryFor(BoundCallProgram)` queried only ProgramNames +
ExternalNames, so `>>TURN EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND CHECKING ON` produced no `BoundEcChecked` wrapper and the emitter
had nothing to work from; a user-FUNCTION activation now also queries `FunctionActivationNames` (§8.4.3.2.4 GR6b →
GR6f). ⚠ The note's stated repro for that defect — a UDF miss while evaluating a CALL argument — does NOT
reproduce on today's tree: `UdfBinder.UdfWrapCalls` hoists the activation out of the statement, so it never runs
inside the CALL's `try`; its live carrier is a UDF miss inside the callee, i.e. the GR3i case again. Two facts
that were prose are now structure: GR3h item 1's family partition is `CobolCallException.IsProgramOrExternal`,
asked by both the compile-time split and the emitted runtime filter, and the carriable name set is
`CobolCallException.CarriedNames`, re-derived from the raise sites by the new `CallExceptionCarrierDriftTests`
(its failure branch fired once before the list was restored). A stale line fell out of the same sweep: the
carrier's class doc still claimed EC-PROGRAM-ARG-OMITTED travels on it, which stopped being true at PB133.
`GR-14.9.4.4-L2.1`/`-L2.2`/`-L2.3` PARTIAL → CONFORMS; goldens `2023/pb233_call_exception_partition` plus five new
`ExceptionConditionConformanceTests` (three of them `AssertFatal` arms a corpus golden cannot express). No
diagnostic code was needed — every arm is a runtime disposition rule — so COBOLNET1752/1753 return unused.

**PB598 — a size rule written for an item, enforced against a condition-name, and the two-parameter shape that
let it happen.** `01 XV PIC X. 88 XC VALUE "cd".` was COBOLNET1740 where ISO/IEC 1989:2023 makes it a legal,
permanently-false condition; the national and boolean twins (`88 NC VALUE N"ABC".` on `PIC N(2)`,
`88 BC VALUE B"101".` on `PIC 1(2) USAGE BIT`) were COBOLNET0898 and had been wrong since those arms were written
— only the alphanumeric one ever surfaced, as GnuCOBOL differential flip `syn_misc:388`, because the corpus
carries no oversize national or boolean level-88 literal (0 of 1,611 members). ⛔ The rules name their subjects
and the code did not. §13.18.63.3 SR4/SR5/SR10 are each a CLASS sentence plus a SIZE sentence, and the size
sentence bounds exactly two subjects — "an elementary item" ("the size indicated by an **explicit** PICTURE

condition-name entry "no true concept of level", so it is neither of §8.5.1.3.1's subdivisions; and §13.18.63.4
GR19 gives it its conditional variable's characteristics only *implicitly* — precisely what "explicit" excludes.
The standard even says what an oversize one MEANS, which a size rule would make dead text: §8.8.4.5.3 item 2 sends

**PB237 — the program-prototype registry lands whole; the CALL Format-2 bracket was mis-transcribed in a code

Two things fall out of that row and neither was predictable from §14.

**The data description clauses are roughly twice as defective as the statements.** A §14 batch closed a quarter of its rules outright; this one closed a sixth, and its GAP delta per adjudicated rule is HALF b2's. The reason is visible in the notes rather than in the numbers: §13.18's rules are overwhelmingly about the SHAPE of a declaration — which clauses may be combined, what a group-level clause does to its subordinates, what a picture character-string may contain — and this compiler's data binder is a per-entry `foreach` over clause kinds. It has almost no machinery for a rule whose subject is a RELATION between entries, so the whole class of "applies to each elementary item in the group" rules lands on the same missing arm.

**The yield estimate should be revised UP for the data division and the projection re-run.** 0.36 notes/rule was fitted on §14; §13 returns 0.42 even after aggressive clustering (104 adjudicator findings + 39 refuter mechanisms → 95 notes, a 40 % reduction by merging one root across files).
